name: Integrations
usage: Use only the parts that apply; delete the others with their tests. Webhooks (src/webhook.mjs): read the raw body with readRawBody(req) (1 MB cap; answer too-large with 413 and Connection: close), take the bare hex HMAC and the timestamp out of the provider's headers (strip a prefix such as 'sha256=' or split 't=…,v1=…' first), then const { release } = await verifyWebhook({ secrets, body, signature, timestamp, replay }) with the shared secret from config (WEBHOOK_SECRET, never in the repo; list two while rotating) and one memoryReplayStore() per process, or a shared store with the same claim(key, expiresAtMs) and release(key) contract (a unique-key insert and a delete) when the app runs more than one instance. It checks an HMAC-SHA256 over '<timestamp>.<raw body>' in constant time, a 5-minute window and replays. Answer 400 for signature-missing, signature-invalid, timestamp-invalid, stale and replayed, and 503 for replay-store-full (the sender retries). Parse JSON only after it passes. If processing then fails and you answer 5xx, call release() first so the provider's resend is accepted. A provider with its own signing scheme (Stripe, Razorpay) uses its official verifier instead, plus the window where the provider signs a timestamp, and the event ledger for dedupe. Payment events (src/events.mjs): createEventLedger({ rank, store }) and apply({ id, objectId, type, version }, handler): version is the provider's event time or sequence per object, rank orders event types that share a version (later states higher); duplicates and events older than the object's last applied one are not applied, and a failing handler records nothing so the provider's retry is applied. With more than one instance, give it a database store: transaction(fn) plus hasEvent/lastOrder/commit taking the transaction (applied event ids under a unique key, the last order per object read with SELECT … FOR UPDATE), and write in the handler through the transaction it is given, so the effect and the record commit together. Cache (src/cache.mjs): createCache({ ttlMs }) — every entry expires; read with get(key, loader) and change data only through write(keys, writer), which drops the keys before and after the write so no read returns the old value afterwards. Third-party tokens (src/token-vault.mjs): createTokenVault({ keys: loadTokenKeys(TOKEN_KEYS), scopes }) with TOKEN_KEYS='<id>:<32-byte base64 key>' from the server's secret store (openssl rand -base64 32; put the new key first to rotate, then rewrap() stored records before removing the old key; rewrap needs the record's scopes still declared and the token not expired) and scopes = the least scopes the app needs per provider; ask the provider for scopesFor(provider, need) only, seal() what it returns (a broader grant is refused), store the record, and open(record, { provider, owner, need }) only for the signed-in owner. Never log a token, a key or a signature.
